# Performance Requirements Quality Checklist: S3-Compatible Local Storage Server

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of performance-related requirements (streaming, startup/lifecycle, scanner & listing, management plane & metrics, load scenarios, constitution-gated benchmarks) before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Data Plane: Streaming & Memory

- [x] CHK001 Is the SC-003 acceptance criterion for "memory usage stays flat" quantified — e.g., is the measurement methodology (peak RSS vs. object size, buffer bound, test harness) defined anywhere in spec/plan? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK002 Is the bounded-buffer streaming requirement (FR-010) consistently extended to ALL transfer paths — single upload/download, multipart part upload and assembly, CopyObject, and abort cleanup — or does it only cover basic get/put? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010/FR-014/FR-015]
- [x] CHK003 Are ranged GET (partial object read) performance requirements defined — e.g., that a Range request reads only the requested byte window rather than the whole object? [Gap, Coverage]
- [x] CHK004 Is a performance requirement defined for concurrent writes to the same object (FR-011 last-write-wins) — e.g., expected behavior/throughput under N simultaneous writers, or is this intentionally unconstrained? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK005 Is the design ceiling (hundreds of GB to a few TB per root) reflected in streaming requirements — i.e., are the same flat-memory guarantees explicitly required for objects beyond 1 GB (SC-003's test size)? [Consistency, Spec §SC-003/Assumptions]

## Startup & Lifecycle

- [x] CHK006 Is SC-005's measurement condition defined — what counts as "ready" (bind, config load, scanner start?), what is a "typical machine", and is the 1-second budget allocated to each startup phase? [Clarity, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK007 Do the FR-024 "never blocks startup" scanner requirement and SC-005's 1-second readiness target agree — is there a requirement stating the scanner may NOT consume startup time, or are they silently competing? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024/SC-005]
- [x] CHK008 Is the graceful-shutdown drain budget quantified in the requirements — plan.md says "bounded (10 s) in-flight drain" but spec FR-018 only says "bounded" — is the bound stated in the requirement layer? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK009 Is a requirement defined for the shutdown behavior of in-flight background work (scanner, sweep) — FR-024 says "aborting quietly on shutdown", but is there any requirement about restart-resume behavior (scan progress loss, partial sweep state)? [Recovery, Gap, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK010 Is the background sweep's runtime cost bounded in the requirements — the sweep (temps 24 h, multipart 7 d) scans the tree asynchronously; is there a requirement preventing it from contending with request traffic, or is that only specified for the scanner? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-014/FR-024]

## Scanner & Listing

- [x] CHK011 Is the cold-listing cost of FR-022 quantified — the "one-time full-content pass over externally-added files" is accepted, but is there a requirement stating a bound (e.g., per-object scan cost, listing latency under the design ceiling, or a documented decision that none exists)? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK012 Is the scanner's rate-limiting requirement specified concretely — FR-024 says "configurable and rate-limitable", but are the rate-cap unit, default, and range defined (or deferred to the `[scanner]` contract keys `delay`/`max_wait`/`cycle`)? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK013 Is the "yields to request traffic" requirement (FR-024) defined measurably — how is yielding detected/verified (max added request latency, scheduler priority, pause semantics)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK014 Is a listing latency requirement defined for large buckets — with the design ceiling of "hundreds of thousands of objects per bucket", are prefix/delimiter list (FR-004) and pagination expected to stay within any latency bound, or is that deliberately unspecified? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK015 Are FR-013 (files appear immediately without restart) and FR-024 (background pre-computation) consistent on first-listing behavior — does the spec state what a client sees between the file appearing and the scanner finishing its ETag? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013/FR-022/FR-024]

## Management Plane & Metrics

- [x] CHK016 Does SC-007's 1-second round-trip cover all management endpoints (status, stop, metrics, openapi), including under load from a full-scan gauge computation, or only status/stop? [Coverage, Spec §SC-007]
- [x] CHK017 Is the full-scan metric TTL quantified in the requirement layer — FR-019 says "TTL-cached full scans" but the 30 s value appears only in plan.md; is the TTL (or a documented decision about it) stated in requirements? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK018 Is a requirement defined for the cost of metrics collection on the data plane — e.g., that scrape/recording of the three metric layers must not measurably degrade request handling, or that TTL-cached gauges bound that cost at the design ceiling? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK019 Is the access-log overhead (FR-017 duration logging on every request) bounded by any requirement — log IO behavior under sustained traffic, ability to disable/redirect without data-plane impact? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-017]

## Load & Scale Scenarios

- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for concurrent client scenarios — multiple S3 clients uploading/downloading simultaneously (streaming + temp-file + rename path under concurrency), or is concurrency behavior only covered by the last-write-wins edge case? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-003/FR-011]
- [x] CHK021 Are performance expectations defined for many-small-objects workloads — the ETag meta store, listings, and scanner behavior under "hundreds of thousands of objects" (single `meta.redb` file, no per-entry file tax; the redb migration removes the fan-out layout and the meta-file count) — or does the design ceiling leave this open? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §Assumptions/FR-022]
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for degraded environments — slow disks, limited memory, or a busy machine where the scanner/sweep contend for IO — including what degrades gracefully vs. what fails? [Coverage, Gap, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK023 Are boundary-size performance behaviors specified — zero-byte objects and very large objects are handled (FR-011 edge cases), but is there any requirement on their performance characteristics (e.g., zero-byte uploads must not traverse the full streaming path)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK024 Is there a requirement covering request-level timeout/duration behavior under IO stall (e.g., a file becomes unreadable mid-stream) — what the client sees and whether the server stays responsive — or is this only implied by the mid-operation error edge case? [Exception Flow, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Gates (Constitution V)

- [x] CHK025 Is the constitution-V benchmark requirement mapped to concrete requirements — which hot paths (streaming write/read, listing, multipart assembly) MUST have criterion benchmarks, and is the "MUST NOT regress without discussion" rule operationalized in spec/plan (e.g., what counts as a regression, who approves)? [Completeness, plan.md Testing, research.md §13]
- [x] CHK026 Is "no hidden allocations" (constitution V) made verifiable — are the hot paths where allocation-freedom is required enumerated, or is the criterion left as a general principle without testable scope? [Clarity, Gap, Constitution V]
- [x] CHK027 Is the "no performance promises beyond the design ceiling" assumption (spec Assumptions) applied consistently — do all success criteria and NFRs (SC-003/005/007, FR-024) state their scope, or do any imply unbounded-scale guarantees? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items without an explicit `[Spec §…]` reference carry `[Gap]`/`[Recovery]`/`[Exception Flow]`/`[Edge Case]` markers — they probe requirement dimensions absent from the current spec

### Review Resolution (2026-08-22)

All 27 items reviewed and satisfied (reviewer-confirmed via grilling session; standards: full scope, standard PR review depth, extended load scenarios). Amendments applied:

- **spec.md** — FR-010 (streaming guarantee covers all transfer paths incl. ranged reads); SC-005 (readiness definition — data plane bound and accepting; background work MAY continue after readiness, MUST NOT delay it); FR-024 (readiness cross-reference); FR-018 (10 s drain bound); FR-019 (30 s TTL + recording-overhead bound); FR-022 (no listing latency bound within design ceiling; listings always correct and complete); FR-014 (sweep yields to request traffic like the scanner); Assumptions Usage model (no throughput/latency guarantees under concurrent clients, many-small-object workloads, or degraded hardware — correctness only). A 2026-08-22 performance-review session was added to the spec's Clarifications.
- **plan.md** — Testing (criterion benchmark set — streaming write/read, multipart assembly, prefix/delimiter listing; regression = mean slowdown > 10 % vs. recorded baselines, requiring a documented decision and reviewer approval; SC-003 verified via 1 GB stream + peak-RSS sampling); Constraints (allocation discipline scoped to streaming hot paths — bounded buffers, no per-object allocation).

Items satisfied as **intentional non-goals** (documented here; no new requirements added): CHK004 (concurrent-write throughput — Assumptions non-goal statement), CHK009 (no restart-resume for background work — mtime-idempotent by design), CHK019 (access-log overhead — async tracing logging with configurable destination), CHK023 (zero-byte fast path — implementation detail).

Items satisfied by existing requirement/contract text without amendment: CHK005 (FR-010 "regardless of object size"), CHK012 (scanner rate keys/defaults `delay`/`max_wait`/`cycle` in `contracts/config.md`), CHK013 (yielding kept qualitative; plan-level integration test — cold listing under concurrent traffic), CHK016 (SC-007 correctly scoped to status/stop; metrics governed by the TTL cache), CHK024 (mid-operation failure edge case), CHK027 (Assumptions ceiling scope).

Tensions resolved: FR-022's accepted cold-listing cost vs. FR-024's scanner guarantee (CHK011/CHK015) — resolved by FR-022's declarative no-bound statement; plan/contract-only quantifications (10 s drain, 30 s TTL) are now stated in the requirement layer (CHK008/CHK017).
